LEAD | program: shortwin | function: init_uva | bug_class: hardening-existing-uva-validation | group_key: shortwin | init_uva | hardening-existing-uva-validation
title: Existing UVAs skip full validation during market creation
file: programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:1161
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_curve.rs:1047; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:469; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_curve.rs:766; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/create_market.rs:430
code_smells: Both init_uva helpers accept an existing venue-owned, nonempty UVA without decoding its discriminator or user field.
trace: create_market derives the UVA from the trader and calls init_uva below creator: Signer. Each helper checks the program, UVA key, and event authority. The existing-account branch then checks only the owner and nonempty data. The trading paths decode the UVA and require its user to equal the trader. The current venue PDA rules prevent outsiders from populating a different account type or user there. No current wrong-user creation path was proved.
description: A future venue layout change can make listing accept an invalid UVA that later trades reject.
fix: Decode an existing UVA and require its user to equal the trader before the helper returns.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: sweep_trader | bug_class: external-cashback-recovery-dependency | group_key: shortwin | sweep_trader | external-cashback-recovery-dependency
title: Cashback cleanup depends on external claim instructions
file: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:246
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/engine/lender.rs:197; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:791; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:339
code_smells: sweep_trader sets the rewards bit only after external cashback accounts report no claimable balance.
trace: rewards_required follows the pump UVA or pump venue. SweepTrader reads the keyed pump UVA and, on PumpSwap, its WSOL ATA. A positive claimable amount leaves rewards_clear false, so the VenueRewards sweep does not set WIPE_REWARDS_CLAIMED. The function never invokes the venue claim itself; callers must bundle the external permissionless claim described by its module. The source asserts current venue claims work without the trader signature. This static pass did not inspect deployed venue bytecode or prove an upgrade that disables those claims. The dependency concerns recovery of outstanding cashback after such a change.
description: A future venue change that disables cashback claims can leave deposits waiting for the rewards bit after a pool wipe.
fix: Define and test a recovery path for outstanding cashback when an external claim stops working.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: elf_fingerprint_of | bug_class: hardening-truncated-elf-digest | group_key: shortwin | elf_fingerprint_of | hardening-truncated-elf-digest
title: The guard stores twelve bytes of each ELF hash
file: programs/shortwin/src/state/venue_guard.rs:47
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/state/venue_guard.rs:52; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/flag_venue_upgraded.rs:100; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/revalidate_venue.rs:104
code_smells: elf_fingerprint_of retains 12 bytes, and is_upgrade compares only that prefix after ProgramData grows.
trace: GUARD_ELF_LEN=12 yields a 96-bit stored fingerprint. A venue authority that chooses both ELFs can seek a pair with the same prefix, obtain review of one, then extend and replace it with the other. The generic chosen-pair work is about 2^48 hashes; this review supplies no collision, practical search budget, or usable malicious ELF pair. The full 32-byte reviewed hash is present at revalidation but not retained.
description: A venue authority can seek two ELF files with one stored fingerprint; this review does not prove a practical collision.
fix: Store and compare the full SHA-256 digest during venue revalidation and upgrade checks.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: read_state_boxed_for_exit | bug_class: curve-risk-fee-at-spot | group_key: shortwin | read_state_boxed_for_exit | curve-risk-fee-at-spot
location: programs/shortwin/src/venues/mod.rs:1078-1086; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_curve.rs:425-485; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/liquidate.rs:337-354; services/keeper/src/decide.rs:285-303.
title: Curve risk quotes retain the fee resolved at spot
code_smells: Exit reads request the EMA fee only for PumpSwap, while curve pricing resolves its ordinary fee from live reserves.
assumption: A curve's live fee is an adequate basis for hypothetical risk quotes throughout the exit check.
proof: read_state_boxed_for_exit sets ema_fee only when kind==PumpSwap. The curve reader resolves fees::pump_curve(live.vt,live.vq,...) and leaves fee_ppm_at_ema at u32::MAX without ema_fee. liquidate::assess and the keeper carry state.quoter().capped(cap) into the EMA and robust-spot quotes. Thus those risk quotes retain a live-tier input even when their reserve reference is historical. No concrete supported fee-tier movement plus a wrong exit decision was established in this bounded review.
guards: The position's hard fee cap, completed-bucket reference, persistence, warm-up and budget checks still apply. The source explicitly makes the extra EMA calculation PumpSwap-only; extending it to curves needs a policy decision and a concrete economic trace.
description: Curve exits use a live fee for historical risk quotes; the review does not prove that a supported tier change causes a wrong exit.
next_check: Trace a real curve fee schedule across a reachable tier boundary and compare the full liquidation and settlement predicates before proposing any change.

location: programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:1161; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_curve.rs:1047
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/create_market.rs:430; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:469
title: Existing Pump UVAs skip full validation at listing
boundary: The existing UVA branch of each create_market CPI helper.
code_smells: Both helpers accept the expected UVA key when its owner matches the venue and its data is nonempty.
proof: Neither existing-account branch checks the UVA discriminator, minimum layout, or stored user. Both return Ok immediately. The PumpSwap trade check later calls uva_ok, which parses the complete UVA and compares u.user with market.trader.
guards_and_limits: create_market derives the UVA from the canonical trader PDA. Both helpers check the exact fixed executable venue program and event authority. The creator signs as payer. An outsider cannot write arbitrary data at this venue PDA. No current account substitution or funds loss was proved. A changed venue layout could make listing succeed while later trading fails.
description: Listing accepts an existing UVA after only its key, owner, and nonempty-data checks; a future venue layout can pass listing but fail trading.
fix: Validate the existing UVA discriminator, layout, and user before the helper returns success.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: sweep_trader | bug_class: external-cashback-recovery-dependency | group_key: shortwin | sweep_trader | external-cashback-recovery-dependency
location: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:248; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:334; programs/shortwin/src/engine/lender.rs:202
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/deposit.rs:152; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:2027
title: Cashback cleanup depends on external claim instructions
boundary: The trader's authenticated Pump UVA and PumpSwap cashback ATA in sweep_trader's remaining accounts.
code_smells: The sweep requires empty external cashback accounts before it sets WIPE_REWARDS_CLAIMED, but it cannot claim the cashback itself.
proof: With total_shares = 0, wipe_swept = 0, and one claimable cashback unit, rewards_clear is false. sweep_trader sets the trader-swept bit but skips SweepSource::VenueRewards. rewards_required remains true on pump venues and on any market that retains pump_uva. deposit passes that requirement into the math pool, which rejects a missing reward bit with WipeSweepPending. Only an external claim that removes the cashback can enable the next sweep to set the bit.
guards_and_limits: Current documented Pump and PumpSwap claim instructions accept an unsigned trader. The source describes a working external claim plus sweep sequence. This review did not prove a current pause, upgrade, or account state that permanently prevents those claims. This lead concerns the dependency when that external interface stops working. Sweeps constrain every cashback key to the market cache; the caller cannot substitute an empty account.
description: Deposits still need external cashback claims after a wipe; this review did not prove a current state that permanently blocks those claims.
fix: Define a bounded recovery path for external rewards that remain unclaimable after a venue interface change.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: parse | bug_class: hardening-vault-authority-unchecked | group_key: shortwin | parse | hardening-vault-authority-unchecked
location: programs/shortwin/src/venues/raydium_cpmm.rs:169; programs/shortwin/src/venues/raydium_v4.rs:146
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/venues/raydium_cpmm.rs:346; programs/shortwin/src/venues/raydium_v4.rs:248
title: The Raydium readers omit vault authority checks
boundary: Authenticated Raydium ReadSet vaults in the normal live-state parsers.
code_smells: Both parsers check account programs, pool-recorded keys, and token mints, but they omit each token account's authority.
proof: raydium_cpmm::parse compares v0.mint and v1.mint with the pool fields, then constructs Parsed without comparing their owner fields. raydium_v4::parse does the same for coin and pc. Their verify functions separately require t.owner == the compiled Raydium authority at listing and candidate adoption.
guards_and_limits: The live ReadSet keys come from the authenticated market cache, and initial adoption checks authorities. A caller cannot alter another program's token authority or substitute another key. No current external instruction that changes a listed vault's authority was established. A future venue change could make the normal readers accept balances the venue cannot spend.
description: The live Raydium readers omit vault authority checks; a future authority change can make them accept reserves that the venue cannot spend.
fix: Require the compiled venue authority in both live vault parsers.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: elf_fingerprint_of | bug_class: hardening-truncated-elf-digest | group_key: shortwin | elf_fingerprint_of | hardening-truncated-elf-digest
location: programs/shortwin/src/state/venue_guard.rs:48; programs/shortwin/src/state/venue_guard.rs:52
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/flag_venue_upgraded.rs:107
title: The guard keeps twelve bytes of the ELF hash
boundary: The fingerprint used to distinguish a ProgramData extension from an upgrade after the account grows.
code_smells: elf_fingerprint_of copies only the first 12 bytes of the SHA-256 digest into persisted state.
proof: GUARD_ELF_LEN is 12. elf_fingerprint_of iterates over that 12-byte destination, so bytes 12 through 31 never participate in the later comparison.
guards_and_limits: A fixed reviewed fingerprint requires a generic 96-bit second-preimage search. An actor who chooses both executable versions has a generic 48-bit collision bound. The attacker also needs a valid deployable executable, authority to upgrade the venue, and an account-length change. No colliding pair or present exploit was constructed. This is separate from the proven empty-fingerprint path.
description: The guard stores only twelve hash bytes; this review did not produce two valid executables that share those bytes.
fix: Store and compare the full SHA-256 digest through an explicit account-layout migration.

LEAD | program: shortwin-math | function: pump_curve | bug_class: hardening-fixed-supply-fee-basis | group_key: shortwin-math | pump_curve | hardening-fixed-supply-fee-basis
file: crates/shortwin-math/src/fees.rs:45-51,164-165,177-202; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_curve.rs:425-484; crates/shortwin-math/src/quote/straddle.rs:183-195
Title: Curve quotes retain the original supply for fee tiers
seam: boundary×invariant
code_smells: The normal curve resolver uses PUMP_CURVE_MCAP_SUPPLY instead of the mint's live supply. A burn can move the live market cap across a fee threshold.
description: The curve resolver can choose the wrong fee after a supply burn if the venue adds multiple fee tiers; the present schedule prevents this.
path: A token holder burns circulating tokens → a future multi-tier schedule separates the fixed and live market caps → pump_curve selects the fixed-supply tier → normal curve quotes use that fee.
proof: fees.rs defines PUMP_CURVE_MCAP_SUPPLY = 1_000_000_000_000_000 and passes it to curve_fees_at. That helper computes floor(vq * supply / vt), then selects the last tier whose threshold is at most the result. For vt = 300_000_000_000_000, vq = 100_000_000_000, and live supply = 600_000_000_000_000, the fixed market cap is 333_333_333_333 lamports and the live market cap is 200_000_000_000. A hypothetical threshold of 250_000_000_000 separates them. If the lower tier has a 125 bps protocol fee and the higher tier has 100 bps, the normal resolver returns 100 bps while the live-supply resolver returns 125 bps. For q = 1_000_000_000_000, the normal curve quote has net = ceil(q * vq / (vt - q)) + 1 = 334_448_162. Its cost is 337_792_644 at 100 bps and 338_628_765 at 125 bps, a difference of 836_121 lamports. This is a pure integer calculation, not execution evidence.
caller_evidence: pricing_inputs receives supply but calls fees::pump_curve for its ordinary fees and its EMA fee. It separately calls pump_curve_at_supply for synthetic_fees. curve_synthetic retains ordinary curve_fees when q <= state.rt. Thus the existing synthetic correction does not change the ordinary branch.
guards_and_limitations: fees.rs:46-52 explicitly states that the current curve schedule has one tier at threshold zero. That condition makes the two market-cap bases select the same tier today. Owner-checked external fee data controls the schedule. This review did not inspect live accounts or prove an active multi-tier deployment. The open's min_notional, margin and fee gates do not select the missing supply basis, but they do prevent tiny notional and insufficient margin inputs. A trade CPI can reject an inadequate maximum input. This item remains a hardening lead, not an active exploit finding.
impact: A future fee threshold can cause a normal quote to differ from the venue charge after a burn. The difference can affect trade bounds and risk values that use that quote.
fix: Pass the verified live supply to normal curve fee resolution and use the same basis for the EMA fee.
confidence: high that the bases differ in code; conditional reachability because the source states one current tier.
related_scope: The adapter call is supporting evidence for this shared-library cause. This block does not assert a separate synthetic-fee gate defect.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: sweep_trader | bug_class: external-cashback-recovery-dependency | group_key: shortwin | sweep_trader | external-cashback-recovery-dependency
title: Cashback cleanup depends on external claim instructions
location: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:129-135, 248-263, 334-350, 371-386; programs/shortwin/src/engine/lender.rs:202-208; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:791-803; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:2025-2035
seam: periphery×first-principles
code_smells: The reward-clear bit depends on external cashback accounts that this sweep cannot empty.
description: A failed external cashback claim can keep deposits blocked after a wipe; this review does not prove a current failure.
trace: A wipe or last-share withdrawal clears sweep flags → sweep_trader finds outstanding cashback → the reward bit stays clear → deposit fails WipeSweepPending.
proof: rewards_required returns true for a stored pump UVA or any pump venue. sweep_trader requires the pump UVA's excess lamports to be zero and, on PumpSwap, its cashback WSOL ATA to be empty. The sweep reads those accounts but does not transfer their balances. Its own trader cleanup therefore cannot set WIPE_REWARDS_CLAIMED while external cashback remains. The documented recovery calls pump or PumpSwap claim_cashback before sweep_trader. A program failure that prevents that external claim leaves no clearing path in the reviewed short.win instructions.
guards: Valid external claims are permissionless and can be bundled with the sweep. Missing external accounts normally mean no cashback, so a missing empty account alone does not prove a block. Existing balances remain assigned to the prior lenders; bypassing the bit would transfer their value to later holders. This issue concerns dependence on an unavailable claim, not missing signer authorization.
limitations: No external claim failure or reachable malicious external state was verified. The source comments state that deployed claim paths work; their cited runtime tests were not rerun. This remains a dependency lead, not a proven deposit outage.
fix_direction: Document and validate recovery when the external claim interface changes; preserve the prior holders' cashback entitlement in any fallback.
